title: `st.camera_input` disabled on mobile + docs.streamlit.io is DOWN
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When using `st.camera_input` on a deployed HTTPS Streamlit app from a mobile phone, it shows this message just like in localhost: The widget should just ask for permission from the browser then the phone, but it doesn't. AND the whole docs.streamlit.app is DOWN, so I can't even click the "Learn how to allow access" link. Can you please solve this problem ASAP because my app depends on it. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python ``` ### Steps To Reproduce _No response_ ### Expected Behavior Ask for camera access and open it on mobile phones. ### Current Behavior DOESN'T Ask for camera access and open it on mobile phones. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.58 - Python version: - Operating System: - Browser: ### Additional Information _No response_

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15905)

This reports that `st.camera_input` on a deployed HTTPS app viewed from a mobile phone stays on the *"This app would like to use your camera. Learn how to allow access."* prompt and never triggers the browser's camera-permission request.

Looking at the frontend, that message is the `AskForCameraPermission` view in `WebcamComponent.tsx`. It is shown whenever `webcamPermission !== WebcamPermission.SUCCESS`, and the state only flips to `SUCCESS` when `react-webcam`'s `onUserMedia` callback fires (i.e. `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia()` resolves). If `getUserMedia()` never prompts/resolves on the device, the widget appears "disabled" and stuck on this message. Note that the `ERROR` path (`onUserMediaError`) renders the *exact same* message as the pending state, so a blocked/denied/failed camera is visually indistinguishable from "still waiting" — a UX gap worth addressing.

The most common environmental triggers for this (even over HTTPS) are: (1) the app being embedded in an `iframe` without `allow="camera; microphone"` (Permissions Policy blocks `getUserMedia` silently); (2) the page not actually being a *secure context* on the phone (invalid/self-signed TLS cert, or LAN-IP over HTTP), which mobile browsers block without a visible prompt; or (3) camera access previously denied for that site/browser at the OS/browser level. The reporter should confirm whether the app is embedded and whether other camera sites work in the same mobile browser. The separate "docs.streamlit.io is DOWN" note refers to the `CAMERA_PERMISSION_URL` target (`docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/using-streamlit/enable-camera`); that would be a transient docs-hosting outage rather than a library bug.

### Related Issues

- [#5075 – Switching camera stuck on permissions](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5075) — Confirmed bug where `st.camera_input` gets stuck in a permissions loop on some mobile devices; closest match to this permission/mobile behavior.
- [#9447 – st.camera_input - Image size with low resolution at small pages](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9447) — Another confirmed, mobile-specific `st.camera_input` issue; useful shared context for camera behavior on phones.
- [#12477 – Allow uploading images from camera in st.chat_input](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12477) — Related mobile camera-capture request (enhancement, not a duplicate).
